body:
# Actual native sheet-detachment repair — UNRUN

Request46a76741-5eb0-4d43-a569-0a311b80347e. Preserve BOTH failed GUI candidates: initial5ad1cbcc silently lost Replace; exact358d19d3857af55bff07f1b8db69a17c48006320 passed17save+4load+3adjacent/direct0 but actual existing-path Save As reported 'Another sheet is still attached to the document window'. No candidate acceptance follows from those unit passes.

Separate checkpoints on existing codex/document-save-settlement:
- tests772896a9: three new native-detachment ordering/cancel/window-loss tests; existing fake fixture models a native detach event separately from SwiftUI dismissal. All UNRUN (20 save cases total).
- productdbe55346: captured sheet/parent detachment handoff in DocumentWorkspace.swift and DocumentSheets.swift.
- productd91363a2: notification-token lifetime cleanup if workspace disappears.

A zero-sized NSViewRepresentable inside the actual Save As content captures its hosting NSWindow by request ID. At existing-file Save, before clearing presentedSaveAs, require captured parent.attachedSheet === captured sheet AND sheet.sheetParent === parent. Install parent didEndSheet and willClose observers before triggering dismissal; retain those actual windows in a request-specific presentation-drain record. Native notification advances only when that exact old sheet has no parent and the captured parent no longer has that sheet attached. Unrelated notification while the old sheet remains attached is ignored. Replace still fails safely if another sheet is attached after the old one leaves. No arbitrary main-actor scheduling, delay, sleep or polling proves detachment.

The transition joins two explicit facts: SwiftUI onDismiss for the claimed ID and actual native detachment. Either order is allowed; both are required before Replace. Duplicate/stale callbacks validate record object identity and request UUID. Cancellation/supersession removes the save operation and its prompt/write continuation, so later detachment cannot open Replace or write. Its separate native presentation-drain observer remains only until old native sheet plus SwiftUI dismissal settle, preventing successor presentation racing that old sheet; it then removes all tokens exactly once. Parent-window loss immediately removes native observation and settles failure; workspace release removes native tokens through an owning RAII token holder. This intentional short-lived drain ownership is distinct from retaining a cancelled save request. No indefinite timers or retry loops.

The requested-versus-content-claimed fix remains: unconsumed requests never take native ownership; begin/cancel/begin without appearance needs no notification. Existing ContentView modifier wiring unchanged. Typed-save results and Layers backend completion unchanged. No AppModel/global Quit/draft finalization changes.

New deterministic tests hold native attachment after SwiftUI dismissal and assert no Replace until injected actual-detach; duplicate native/dismiss callbacks produce one prompt/cleanup; cancellation in that interval settles once and never prompts/writes after detach; window loss removes observer and makes later notification inert. Tests inject event continuations, not native windows or disk work. Production parent/sheet identity checks require actual A GUI validation; fake event tests are not that evidence.

Source inspection/git diff --check only on B. Compilation and every test remain UNRUN here. A must compile and rerun same-path/distinct-path Replace Cancel/acceptance, Escape, cancel/supersession/window-close during teardown, unshown cancellation and source-probe identity capture. Validate didEndSheet notification arrives after captured sheet detaches; if it does not, do not substitute a timer—retain failure evidence and review the native host completion boundary. All older native lifecycle caveats remain until exercised. Normal preview untouched, B resource hold/heartbeat pause/writer preserved, A sole compiler/GUI/main owner.
